newsitem.title: INDIA: India truck strike in 6th day with no end in sight.
newsitem.headline: India truck strike in 6th day with no end in sight.

text.p: Indian truckers, whose six-day strike has paralysed trade and pushed up prices, pressed their campaign against a new tax on Sunday.

"The service tax has to be dropped," S.P. Singh, spokesman for the independent truck owners' group, the All India Motor Transport Congress, told Reuters. "Nothing more or nothing short will pacify us.
"The agitation is now six days old and tomorrow the buses will be off roads in New Delhi in support of the truck owners strike."

The truckers object to a five percent service tax on road transport proposed in the 1997-98 budget of Finance Minister P. Chidambaram. The buget has not yet been approved by parliament, where the United Front government's future stands in doubt because of a falling out with the Congress Party.
The Indian Association of Tour Operators, an association of private local bus operators in New Delhi, said on Saturday it will observe the strike for one day on Monday.
The protest has kept some 2.2 million trucks off the roads, paralysed the movement of goods and disrupted India's foreign trade, which amount to nearly $200 million a day.
Industry officials said shortages had begun to push up prices of rice, wheat and edible oil.
